Welcome to WESTOVER GREEN COMMUNITY SCHOOL AND AUTISM CENTRE
'Every Child. Every day. Every opportunity to belong, achieve and thrive.' The Westover Way: Be safe, be ready, be kind, be respectful.
Welcome
A warm welcome to Westover Green Community School. We are a large primary school near to the town centre of Bridgwater. Our school is organised across 14 classes with 2 classes for each year group from reception to year 6 and we have a specialist base on site for learners with a diagnosis of autism or a communication and interaction need.
We are a forward‑thinking school with innovative leaders and dedicated staff. Our caring and highly skilled team work tirelessly to champion our vision, ‘Every child. Every Day, Every opportunity to belong, achieve and thrive.’ Our staff team are meticulous at removing any potential barriers to learning and nurturing children’s curiosity, and supporting them to become life‑long learners who achieve their full potential.
To help our pupils grow into confident, well‑rounded individuals, we embed The Westover Way into all aspects of school life. We take great pride in our high-quality care, inclusive ethos, and ambitious curriculum, all of which ensure that every child develops a strong sense of who they are.
Despite being close to the town centre, we are fortunate to have a large forest school area featuring a range of native trees and plants, a pond, a mud-kitchen, an outdoor classroom, and a fire pit. Our Forest School is in use every day, all day. Every child in reception, year 1, and our specialist base take part in a weekly forest school session throughout the year. At Westover, we value the importance of outdoor learning as a way to promote children’s health and well-being, while also supporting their personal development, communication skills, and motor control. In addition to whole-class sessions, we also offer small-group forest school interventions for children with an Education, Health and Care Plan, as well as those who may benefit from additional support.
At Westover Green, we are proud to offer a rich programme of enrichment clubs that inspire children’s interests and broaden their experiences beyond the classroom. With a wide range of opportunities such as table tennis, LEGO Club, craft club, cookery club and violin lessons—there is something for every child to enjoy and explore. Our wraparound care further supports families by providing a safe, nurturing environment from 7:30am to 5:30pm, ensuring children are well looked after and engaged throughout and beyond the school day.
In addition to this, we celebrate the arts through our vibrant Westover Performers programme, which brings together children from across the school in show choir, dance, and drama. Our talented pupils work with passion and confidence to create high‑quality performances, and in recent years they have wowed audiences with musical spectaculars such as Matilda and The Wizard of Oz. These opportunities not only showcase our children’s creativity and teamwork but also help them to develop self‑belief, resilience, and a lifelong love of the performing arts.
As proud members of the Futura Learning Partnership, we benefit from being part of a collaborative family of schools. This partnership enables us to share expertise, strengthen professional development, and enrich the opportunities available to our children. Working together across the trust helps us continually improve, ensuring that every child at Westover Green receives the very best education and experiences.
Browse through our website to familiarise yourselves with our school a little better. If you would like any of our information in printed form, just let us know – we’ll be happy to provide it for you.
We warmly encourage visits to our inclusive school, and we urge you to come and visit us when the children are working, so that you can see first-hand the rich learning environment that our staff work so hard to create. Please contact the school office and I will be delighted to take the time to show you and your child around our inclusive school.

All maintained schools must meet the requirements set out in section 78 of the Education Act 2002 and promote the spiritual, moral, social and cultural (SMSC) development of their pupils.
Through ensuring pupils’ SMSC development, schools can also demonstrate they are actively promoting fundamental British values.
Meeting requirements for collective worship, establishing a strong school ethos supported by effective relationships throughout the school, and providing relevant activities beyond the classroom are all ways of ensuring pupils’ SMSC development.
Pupils must be encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance.
It is expected that pupils should understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law. The school’s ethos and teaching, which schools should make parents aware of, should support the rule of English civil and criminal law and schools should not teach anything that undermines it. If schools teach about religious law, particular care should be taken to explore the relationship between state and religious law. Pupils should be made aware of the difference between the law of the land and religious law.

SIAMS - Church schools inspection
The school was originally built by the Elton Family as a Sunday school before becoming a school to support the education of children within the East Clevedon Community. All Saints Church of England Primary School has a Christian foundation that all staff and governors value which is supported by the Bible reference Proverbs 22: 6.
The school’s Christian character influences its approach to educational experiences, the way staff interact with children and parents, the behavioural policy and how religious education lessons are taught.
We hold a daily act of Christian Worship and being locked just opposite the church benefit from a very close working relationship. Children attend a weekly Collective Worship in Church and all main Christian Celebrations are held in church. At times the church building is used by the staff and children to support the curriculum.
The very close working relationship also means that the school rent and use the church hall as a school hall and the Glebe field as a playing field for PE lessons and outside playtimes. During the rebuild of the school, the church was also used to teach in, and hold meetings.
Our Siams inspection (sept 2024) identified the following strengths.
• The clarity of the vision embedded by the school’s inspirational leadership. It empowers all to be ‘inspired to learn’ and become lifelong learners. As a result, the vision has a profound impact on pupils’ wellbeing, behaviour and achievement.
• The school’s curriculum explicitly promotes creativity and curiosity and is highly motivating. In this way, pupils grow in confidence and feelings of self-worth.
• Collective worship is central to life at All Saints. It provides meaningful moments in which all can grow spiritually. This is due to the powerful impact of the vision.
• The school creates a culture of exceptional care and encouragement. This is inspired by the vision of a ‘nurturing environment’, reflecting Christian care for its community. This ensures that adults and pupils are treated well.
• Very effective leadership in religious education (RE) has established a relevant and challenging curriculum which enhances pupils’ learning. As a result, they enjoy learning in RE. This has a positive impact on their understanding of a range of faiths and worldviews including Christianity

At All Saints Church of England Primary School, we are proud of our Christian Foundation which is rooted in our involvement with our local Church - All Saints.
All Saints as a Church School
We value our church foundation and how this makes our school a special place to be.
At All Saints Church of England Primary School, we are proud of our Christian Foundation which is rooted in our involvement with our local Church- All Saints.
Our Siams Inspection Sept 2024) assessed that ‘the school creates a culture of exceptional care and encouragement. This is inspired by the vision of a ‘nurturing environment’, reflecting Christian care for its community. This ensures that adults and pupils are treated well.’
The school was built for the community of East Clevedon and we welcome all pupils and their families of all faiths or none to live out our Vision Statement ‘Inspired to learn’ and to carry out Proverbs 22:6 where, as a community “we start children off on the way they should go and even when they are old they will not turn from it.
Church Links
All Saints Church was founded in 1860 and celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2010.
In 1870 the Church, together with the Diocese of Bath and Wells, built All Saints School.
In those days it started as a Sunday School, but quickly developed into an Infants and Primary school serving this community. The school has been supported by the church ever since.
Across the Diocese, we have some 33,000 children currently in church schools. The added value that the ethos and heritage of church schools contributes has been strongly recognised by different Governments over the years and many parents rightly see them as healthy and good schools.
Our aim here, as we seek to support the school, is to be a friend and resource. Our Church building is used on a daily basis by the school, we have weekly Collective Worship taken by the clergy of the church, whole school services for festivals, we provide 3 Foundation Governors to assist in leading the school and we provide pastoral support when needed. We are pleased that our relationship with the school is warm, strong and supportive.
The Diocese takes as its guiding principal some words of Christ found in John’s Gospel – “I have come that they might have life, and have it to the full”. This is what a healthy and positive partnership between the School and Church feels like and at All Saints Church, we hope that our partnership with All Saints East Clevedon Church of England Primary School contributes to this fulfilment and enjoyment of learning and living.
Fr Noel HectorRector of All Saints Church and Rural Dean of Portishead

Collective Worship
Through our collective worship provision we aim to encourage children’s natural sense of wonder and to develop their qualities of curiosity, celebration, faith and gratitude which form the foundation of the worship of God.
Through this we want to contribute to children’s spiritual, moral and cultural development and enable them to reflect specifically on Christian values and beliefs.
To engage our children and provide a variety of approaches to collective worship, we aim to foster a sense of community and unity within the school.
We aspire to offer children an opportunity for the understanding of God in a way that is individual and appropriate for them, and which allows them to be comfortable in worship.
During our Siams Inspection (sept 2024) it was referenced that: ‘Collective worship is central to the school day and has a significant impact on enabling all to flourish spiritually.’
Collective Worship Policy
Each week we congregate to celebrate our collective worship in All Saints Church led by Father Noel. The positioning of our school enables this regular link and our children respect the church as a place of worship.
Our Collective Worship builds on our school values of; Community, Creativity, Joy, Curiosity and Confidence. Our School
We are a primary academy within the Futura Learning Partnership.
Welcome to All Saints Church of England Primary School.
We are incredibly proud to welcome you to All Saints, a thriving and nurturing primary school at the heart of our community — and now the home of our highly successful preschool. Opening the preschool has been a wonderful milestone for us, giving our youngest learners the very best start to their education in a warm, supportive and inspiring environment.
Within our school, children develop a strong sense of belonging and a vibrant learning community. Positive relationships are at the centre of everything we do. Every child is valued, nurtured and encouraged, while also being challenged academically so they can flourish and achieve their full potential.
Ofsted (2023) recognised our strengths, stating:
“This warm and welcoming school is highly valued by the community it serves. Leaders’ vision to promote pupils’ ‘curiosity and confidence’ threads through all that the school does.”
Creativity and a love of learning lie at the heart of our curriculum. Our pupils immerse themselves enthusiastically in their work, supported by a dedicated and highly experienced staff team; many of whom have been part of All Saints for many years. We are deeply proud of our children’s achievements, our staff’s professionalism, and the strong partnerships we share with families and the wider community.
Our SIAMS inspection (Sept 2024) also highlighted the strength of our ethos:
“All Saints is an exceptionally warm and nurturing community where adults and pupils are treated well… Strong, supportive, collaborative relationships are central to school life.”
All Saints has a rich history. Our Victorian building first opened as a primary school on 28th June 1873, and we were delighted to celebrate 150 years of education in 2023. Between 2016 and 2018 the school underwent significant redevelopment, including a new four‑classroom block, modernised facilities and the addition of Saxby Cottage. Today, our children enjoy spacious classrooms, up‑to‑date technology and a learning environment designed for both comfort and inspiration.
We make full use of every part of our site and are fortunate to rent the Church Hall and the Glebe Field, which provide additional space for play, PE and outdoor learning.
At All Saints, we have high expectations for every child — personally, socially and academically. As a small school, we know our pupils well and help them become confident, capable learners ready for the next stage of their education. Children regularly take part in whole‑school performances and presentations from Reception onwards, helping them grow in confidence and creativity.
School Day:The lower gates open at 8:45am, giving children time to settle with classroom activities before the school day begins at 8:50am. The day ends at 3:20pm.
Paper copies of any information on our website are available on request. Please email: office@allsaintsprimaryschool.org.uk
If you have any questions about our school, please do contact us — I would be delighted to talk with you.

Personal Social Health and Economic Education (PSHE)
Intent statement
The purpose of the Futura Learning Partnership’s PSHE intent is to provide a framework for high quality PSHE education across phases which is accessible to all and ensures that each of our pupils will develop the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to keep themselves healthy, safe and prepared for life and work.
The aim is to ensure our pupils understand more about how to play a positive and successful role within our society, both as a child and as an adult within the future. It should have an impact on both academic and non-academic outcomes for pupils, particularly the most vulnerable and disadvantaged.
The aim is for a holistic PSHE learning journey spanning the pupil’s school career, with a progressive, spiral curriculum that addresses real needs in a rapidly changing world. Our curriculum is ambitious for all and strives to address inclusion and disadvantage in its intent and implementation.

Westover Music Development Plan 2025 – 2026
Music Development Plan 2025 – 2026
Intent
In the Futura Learning Partnership, our intention is that children develop a life-long love of music. Through the musical experiences and opportunities offered to them throughout their education, each child will develop a musical identity which is personal to them, this may be in the form of a performer, composer and/or as an active listener who, in the future, will become a participator in the cultural life of the UK. In EYFS, KS1 and KS2 music acts as an integral part of the school day, be that singing whilst packing up, or listening to a new piece of music whilst walking into assembly. Our music curriculum plan, guided by the EYFS framework and National Curriculum, ensures that all children from EYFS and Year 9 experience a 2 stimulating, practical and holistic curriculum which explores music through singing, performing, composing and listening. Every student in the Futura Trust will have been taught the substantive and disciplinary knowledge required for GCSE Music, and therefore possibly A-Level, should they wish to study Music at KS4 and KS5. Alongside this we encourage all students to develop their musicianship in a variety of extra-curricular activities both in and outside school. Inevitably, the cultural capital of each student will be developed throughout their musical education within the Trust yet each individual school also aims to meet the cultural interests, and needs, of the community in which our schools are based – all musical cultures and welcomed and embraced. We strive to ensure all students find Music an engaging and fulfilling subject in which they embrace the discipline of practice, the challenge of analysis and the excitement of creating and finding their own musical voice.

SEND and Inclusion
You can find all the information you need about our SEND policies.
The school’s SENDCo is Mrs Rachel Mills
We are a fully inclusive school and meet the diverse needs of every child in the school. Our Siams Inspection (Sept 2024) summarised the support of individuals : ‘As a result of far-sighted actions by the leaders and staff, the potential of pupils identified as disadvantaged is being transformed.’
Staff work closely with parents to ensure that children’s needs are quickly and effectively identified and that appropriate support is provided or sought.
We acknowledge that some children will develop special educational needs at some time in their school career. Sometimes these can be met by short term targeted support or adapting learning tasks. For some children, their needs will be met by a range of in class, and additional adult support, at times other educational specialists may be involved.
Children may also require an Individual Education Plan (IEP) drawn up by the class teacher, with the support of the special needs co-coordinator (SENCO), and in consultation with the parents. A close partnership with parents is essential to identify a child’s needs and how to meet those needs. A copy of the Special Educational Needs policy can be found within the documents section below.
The children benefit from additional in-class support from a Teaching Assistant or Learning Support Assistant and sometimes work in small groups out of the classroom environment.
We follow a graduated approach – Assess – Plan – Do and Review
The four main SEND areas are (as identified by the SEND Code of Practice):
1. Communication and Interaction.
2. Cognition and Learning.
3. Social, Emotional and Mental Health difficulties.
4. Physical and/or Sensory Needs.
We identify and focus on these categories for our children who may need additional support.
Our School SENDco is Mrs. Rachel Mills.
Should you wish to contact Mrs. Mills, please phone the school- 01275 874169 or email; office@allsaintsprimaryschool.org.uk

Curriculum
Curriculum
The Futura Curriculum
We inspire our children’s learning through a creative curriculum, ensuring our pupils experience a wide breadth of study and have, by the end of each key stage, long-term memory of an ambitious body of procedural and semantic knowledge. Our progressive curriculum, from 3-19 years ensures that children have the requisite knowledge to proceed to their next year of study, including transition to secondary school.
Our curriculum is ambitious, meeting and often exceeding the national curriculum, for all and strives to address inclusion and disadvantage in its intent and implementation.
At Westover Green, we follow the Futura Curriculum for all subject areas with the exception of science (at Westover we follow the scheme from Plan B); Physical Education (at Westover we follow the REAL PE Scheme) and Modern Foreign Languages (at Westover we have developed our own curriculum for the teaching of French).
For more information of the intent, implementation and impact of each curriculum area, please read Futura Curriculum booklet.
For year group specific curriculum information please refer to the Class Pages or the Curriculum Overviews tab.
Westover Green Curriculum intent statement:
The Westover curriculum will be ambitious and inspirational. It will provide access and entitlement to powerful knowledge, ensuring enjoyment and promoting the very best life chances. It will encapsulate our values:
Our school curriculum draws many elements from the National Primary Curriculum (NPC), although objectives are adapted within our creative approach. Contact the school if you require more detail about a specific aspect of the curriculum or if you would like more information on the National Primary Curriculum (NPC), please click on the link below.
